title: Briakos annotations.js source-identity reconciliation: published byte-count conflict versus SHA-256 prefix match
reconciliation_questions: Was annotations.js unchanged at the exact historical commit already admitted for LinearAInscriptions.js?
Does Git history show the same annotations.js blob spanning the Briakos acquisition date and the historical inscription commit?
Can any repository-visible annotations.js revision at or before 2026-03-01 satisfy the reported byte count 2201442?
Does any such candidate also preserve the reported SHA-256 prefix 7ce1f87a?

decision_rule.HASH_LINEAGE_ADMITTED_BYTE_COUNT_CLASSIF: The exact historical-commit file has the published SHA prefix, Git lineage shows no intervening annotations.js content change around acquisition, and no repository-visible candidate satisfying the published byte count has the published hash prefix. This admits the file only as the strongest repository-backed hash-lineage candidate, not as a byte-count-exact Briakos receipt.
decision_rule.SOURCE_IDENTITY_AMBIGUOUS: Multiple plausible revisions exist or lineage cannot resolve the conflict.
decision_rule.SOURCE_IDENTITY_REJECTED: A different repository-visible candidate satisfies both the published byte count and published hash prefix or otherwise clearly supersedes the historical-commit candidate.
